title: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner's exempt list over misdemeanor charges
dek: The Packers running back was placed on paid leave Sunday following misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He is ineligible to play while the league investigates, forcing Green Bay to adjust its backfield during the 53-man roster cutdown deadline.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL's commissioner's exempt list on August 30, 2026, over misdemeanor charges related to an alleged domestic incident, rendering him ineligible to play in Week 1.
bottom_line: The resolution of Jacobs' criminal case will determine the timeline for any NFL disciplinary ruling and his potential return. Until then, the Packers proceed with Johnson in the backfield while Jacobs' legal proceedings unfold separately from his roster status.
body: The NFL placed Packers running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list on August 30 following misdemeanor charges related to an alleged domestic incident, rendering him ineligible to play in Week 1. The placement came as NFL teams faced a 6 p.m. ET deadline the same day to reduce their rosters to 53 players for the season, per Front Office Sports.

Jacobs faces misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property, per Front Office Sports. The Brown County, Wisconsin District Attorney's Office announced the charges on August 29 after Jacobs was arrested in May on initial charges related to domestic abuse, including felony strangulation and suffocation.

While on the exempt list, Jacobs will be paid his salary but cannot practice with the Packers or attend games, per Front Office Sports. The league allows a player on the exempt list to be present at the club's facility on a reasonable basis for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation, and other permitted non-football activities, according to the same source.

Jacobs and the NFL Players Association have three days after he is formally notified of his placement on the list to appeal the league's decision, per Front Office Sports. A player's paid leave will generally last until a disciplinary ruling is made, which usually comes after the player's criminal case is completed. Any games a player misses while on paid leave are credited toward a possible unpaid suspension, with the player returning pay for the appropriate number of games, Front Office Sports reports.

Jacobs is entering the third season of a four-year, $48 million contract with the Packers. He is a three-time Pro Bowl selection over seven NFL seasons with the Raiders and Packers. Last season, Jacobs ran for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns, per Front Office Sports.

The Packers traded for running back Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers on August 30, per Front Office Sports. Johnson was selected by Pittsburgh in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft out of Iowa, according to CBS Sports. Jacobs' attorneys David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld, and Clarence F. Duchac III stated in a written statement that the placement on the exempt list is an administrative procedure and not a final determination.
